title: Array Assignment and Destructuring
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of array assignment and destructuring in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply array assignment and destructuring in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to unpacking returned values and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Array Assignment and Destructuring through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding array assignment and destructuring helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Array Assignment and Destructuring helps you reason about multiple assignment. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Multiple assignment. Then connect it to Rest assignment using *. The remaining syllabus points—Unpacking returned values—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports array assignment and destructuring. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for array assignment and destructuring using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Unpacking returned values), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain array assignment and destructuring, identify its place in arrays, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
